text.p: Procter & Gamble Co's proposed $1.85 billion acquisition of Tambrands for $50 a share is a positive move for both companies, analysts said on Wednesday.

The acquisition of Tambrands is expected to be neutral to Procter & Gamble's earnings in the first year, J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant said. "But it's a positive psychologically and bodes well for the longer term," Grant added.
Procter & Gamble shares were up 3-1/2 at 119-1/4 at midday, while Tambrands gained 1-7/8 at 48.
"I think it's a great acquisition," said Bear, Stearns analyst Constance Maneaty.

She said if the Tambrands acquisition costs Procter & Gamble "a few pennies" in the first year, the Cincinnati-based consumer products company likely would be able to offset that dilution with its other operations.

Procter & Gamble said earlier the acquisition would be $0.02 to $0.03 per share dilutive in the first year, but it would strive to cover dilution internally. Tambrands was expected to be accretive to results thereafter.
For Tambrands and its Tampax tampon brand, Procter & Gamble will be able to help it accelerate its growth, analysts said.
"P&G can give Tambrands so many resources that would take so much time and money to develop on its own," Maneaty said.
